value.tagline: Parliamentary republic on the Atlantic edge of Europe - coalition politics, PR-STV elections, and a rapidly modernising economy.
value.descriptor: A parliamentary republic where the Taoiseach leads government through a Dáil majority, elected by proportional representation using the Single Transferable Vote across multi-seat constituencies.

upperChamber.name: Seanad Éireann
upperChamber.description: 60 senators - 43 elected from vocational panels, 11 nominated by the Taoiseach, 6 from universities.

lowerChamber.name: Dáil Éireann
lowerChamber.description: 147 TDs elected by PR-STV across multi-seat constituencies (1948 redistribution).

executive.title: Enactment
executive.signNote: Once passed by the Dáil, the bill is enacted into law.

value.upperNote: The Seanad may revise or delay a bill, but the Dáil ultimately prevails. Seanad business is not player-managed.

dissolution.body: The Taoiseach may seek a dissolution of the Dáil; a general election is called and all bills in progress fall.

quirks.title: Dáil supremacy
quirks.body: The Dáil drives all legislation; the Seanad can delay but not block.

quirks.title: Dissolution
quirks.body: A Taoiseach-sought election dissolves the Dáil and ends pending bills.
